review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–167). It has no @[simp] attributes, no simp-set definitions and no rewrite-direction choices. The theorems are conditional implications or equalities with non-trivial hypotheses: `sup_pow_eq_top_of_sup_eq_top`, `pairwise_sup_eq_top_pow`, `ideal_smul_inf_of_sup_eq_top` and `ideal_smul_iInf_of_pairwise_sup_eq_top`. These have hypotheses such as comaximality that simp could not discharge in a useful way. I found no argument that any of them needs a simp attribute. The two private wrappers are unused aliases, so they affect no simp interface. The only simp calls are the `simp` closing the empty-selection case and `simp only [Finset.iInf_insert]`. Both are ordinary, local and terminating uses. I did not check Mathlib for competing simp lemmas, because the file adds no simp rules that could compete. Without running Lean, I can't say whether the empty-case `simp` is fragile.
